- [ASSISTANT_SAID] There are academic requirements for players in the OHL; each team must have an education advisor to ensure players make satisfactory progress towards completing high school.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Players are expected to attend high school and maintain passing grades in all subjects.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The OHL has a scholarship program that rewards players for academic success, offering financial assistance for post-secondary education or vocational training.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Attendance policies require players to attend all team activities, including practices, games, and meetings; missing activities without a valid excuse may lead to disciplinary action.
- [USER] User expressed appreciation for the OHL's emphasis on education and attendance alongside hockey skills.
- [USER] User asked if there are specific grade requirements for players to remain eligible to play.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Players must maintain a minimum of a 60% average in all high school courses to stay eligible in the OHL.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Players falling below the 60% average may be placed on academic probation and must work with their education advisor to improve grades.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] If grades do not improve, players may be suspended from playing until they meet league requirements.

- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Advisors provide academic support, study strategies, and time management tips.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The OHL partners with universities and colleges to provide educational resources and opportunities for players.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Many OHL teams have agreements with local school boards for flexible class schedules and tutoring support.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The OHL is committed to helping players achieve academic success while developing hockey skills.
- [USER] User expressed satisfaction with the league's prioritization of education and academic success.
- [USER] User asked how the OHL handles situations where a player struggles with balancing academic and hockey commitments.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The OHL involves the player's education advisor to develop a plan for better time management and prioritization of academic responsibilities.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Players struggling academically may be placed on academic probation, which could limit their playing time until grades improve.
